title: Jassa Singh Wavers Over the Hidden Treasure

blocks.text: Jassa Singh initially answers Maali Singh in the language of honour, reminding him that the Ramgharias and Ghanaiyas had pledged to share what they captured together. He warns that wealth gained by breaking one's vow cannot remain clean profit, because the stain of dishonour will cling to it longer than the gold itself.

Maali Singh refuses to yield, arguing from possession, kinship, and martial pride instead of from principle. He makes the dispute intensely personal, pressing his brother to choose blood loyalty over the public obligation created by alliance.

That pressure changes the moral register of the story. Jassa Singh's hesitation shows that the treasure is already corrupting judgment, and the page ends on the brink of his surrender to a plan he knows is unworthy.
